name: Button stack
purpose: Holds a screen's main action, and any way out of it, at the bottom of the screen under a divider, where they stay as the content scrolls. Used on screens that ask the user to do something, such as confirm, agree or continue.

origin.notes: The app's ButtonStackView, a primary button over a grouped secondary one, and PrimaryButtonView, the same with one button. The divider is a SwiftUI Divider with strokes.fixedContainer laid over it. The app's UIKit screens have their own, StickyFooterView, with its buttons 4pt apart rather than 8pt.

inputs.content: One or two <govuk-app-button> elements, top to bottom: the main action, as a primary or destructive button, then any way out of it as a grouped secondary button. Give the stack slot="footer" to pin it to the bottom of a <govuk-app-screen>.

rules: Put it in a <govuk-app-screen> with slot="footer", so it stays at the bottom as the content scrolls.
Put the main action first, as a primary button, or a destructive one if it deletes or removes something. Put any way out of it second, as a grouped secondary button, such as Cancel or Not now.
Use no more than two buttons.
Don't use it on a screen with a tab bar: the app hides the tab bar on screens that ask the user to act.

avoid.when: For a lighter action within the content, such as on a card
For an action on the whole screen that doesn't move the journey on, such as Edit
On a top-level screen, with a tab bar
avoid.instead: Put the action on a screen of its own, pushed on top, without the tab bar, and put the button stack there.
